messages.content: Now compare the hotel arrangements for June 9 through 15. I want to know whether both rooms truly work for two adults and a 14-year-old, and I want every required charge included. Compare staying at the coastal hotel all six nights with moving downtown for the last two.

I found comparable refundable two-queen rates at the Bahia Resort Hotel for the coastal stay and the InterContinental San Diego for the waterfront portion. The Bahia can be priced either for all six nights or for Monday through Friday morning, followed by two nights at the InterContinental. I’ll verify occupancy, bedding, taxes, mandatory fees, parking, cancellation terms, and the practical cost of changing hotels before comparing them.
Start with occupancy. I do not want a room that says two queens but only permits two guests.

The Bahia’s Standard Two Queen room permits up to four guests, so two adults and one 14-year-old are allowed with no extra-person charge. The InterContinental’s Classic Two Queen room also permits four guests and does not add a fee for the teenager. In both cases, the quoted category guarantees two queen beds rather than treating the second bed as a request.
How large are they? And is either one a sofa-bed setup?

Neither relies on a sofa bed. The Bahia room is about 300 square feet with two queens. The InterContinental room is approximately 385 square feet with two queens, so it gives the three of you noticeably more floor and luggage space for the final two nights.
All right. Give me the full Bahia cost for six nights first.

For June 9-15, the six-night Bahia quote is $2,214.00 in room charges. Hotel taxes and tourism assessments are $287.82. The mandatory resort charge is $45 per night, or $270.00, plus $35.10 tax. Self-parking is $49 per night for six nights, or $294.00. The complete lodging total is $3,100.92. There is no separate charge for the third guest.
Does that resort charge cover parking? I want to be sure it has not been counted twice.

No. The resort charge and parking are separate. The resort charge covers items such as property Wi-Fi and selected resort activities; self-parking is an additional $49 nightly. The $3,100.92 total includes each charge once.
Now price four nights there and two downtown, including whatever we would actually pay at the second hotel.

Four nights at the Bahia come to $1,476.00 for the room, $191.88 in room taxes and assessments, $180.00 in resort charges, $23.40 tax on those charges, and $196.00 for parking. That subtotal is $2,067.28. Two nights at the InterContinental are $718.00 plus $93.34 in taxes and assessments. It has no mandatory resort or destination charge on this rate, and you would return the car before the downtown stay, so I have added no hotel parking. Its subtotal is $811.34. The complete split-stay lodging cost is $2,878.62.
So the move saves a little over two hundred dollars?
Yes. On lodging alone, the split stay saves $222.30 compared with six nights at the Bahia. It also gives you the larger room downtown for Friday and Saturday nights.
What are the cancellation deadlines? Use San Diego time and tell me what happens after each deadline.

The refundable Bahia rate can be canceled without penalty through 4:00 p.m. Pacific time on June 6. After that, the penalty is one night’s room charge plus applicable tax and the first night’s resort charge. That deadline applies whether you reserve four or six nights. The InterContinental rate can be canceled without penalty through 6:00 p.m. Pacific time on June 11; after that, it charges the first night’s room and tax. Neither option requires a nonrefundable prepayment today.
Walk me through Friday if we split. We had planned to return the rental car that morning and I do not want to lose half the day.

Check out of the Bahia by 11:00 a.m. Friday, load the luggage, and drive to the waterfront hotel. The drive is normally about 15-25 minutes outside the worst traffic. The InterContinental will hold the bags even if the room is not ready, and the downtown rental return is about five minutes away. Allow roughly 75-105 minutes from leaving the Bahia to finishing the car return, including unloading and the short walk back. You could be free for sightseeing around noon if you leave the coast near 10:15.
And if we do not move? We would keep the car until Sunday, correct?

Correct. For a six-night coastal stay, the comparison assumes keeping the rental through Sunday, paying all six nights of Bahia parking, and returning the car at the airport. That avoids the Friday transfer but adds two rental days and keeps you based at Mission Bay for the waterfront evening.
Update the whole-trip comparison, not just the rooms. Keep the flight cost with the checked bag, meals, zoo, gas, and local transportation in it.

Using the current working allowances, the split stay is $6,015.62: $1,454 flights including the expected checked-bag charge, $2,878.62 lodging, $382 rental car, $45 gas, $95 rideshares, $216 zoo admission, and $945 meals. The all-coastal plan is $6,313.92: the same flights, zoo, and meals; $3,100.92 lodging; $498 for the longer rental; $55 gas; and $45 in local transportation. On those assumptions, splitting the stay lowers the complete working trip total by $298.30.
Is anything missing from those totals that could make the downtown option look cheaper than it really is?

The split total includes both hotels’ mandatory charges, four nights of coastal parking, the Friday hotel transfer using the rental car, the downtown car return, and rideshares after the return. It does not include optional valet parking, room upgrades, hotel dining, tips, a special Friday dinner, or another paid activity. The same exclusions apply to the all-coastal total, so the comparison is consistent.
Which structure would you choose, given that Friday is supposed to be our waterfront evening? Do not reserve either one yet.

I would use the four-night coastal plus two-night waterfront structure. It saves about $298 across the trip, provides a larger room for the last two nights, eliminates the resort charge and parking after Friday, and puts you in walking distance for the waterfront evening. The tradeoff is roughly 75-105 minutes Friday morning to move bags and return the car. Both room types accommodate all three of you in two queen beds. Nothing has been reserved; the remaining decisions are whether that Friday transfer is worth the savings and whether to add an allowance for the waterfront dinner or another paid activity.
